Here’s a concise overview of Ayala Malls Manila Bay based on generally available, widely reported information.

What it is
- A large lifestyle mall developed and operated by Ayala Malls.
- Located in Aseana City, Parañaque, Metro Manila, near the Mall of Asia/Entertainment City area (close to Solaire, City of Dreams, and Okada; along/near major roads like Macapagal Boulevard, Asean Avenue, and Diokno Boulevard).
- Soft-opened in late September 2019.

Scale and layout
- Among the biggest malls in the Ayala Malls portfolio.
- Multi-level indoor mall with extensive parking and al fresco areas. (Exact floor area and parking counts aren’t consistently published; figures can vary by source.)

Notable features
- Japan Town and Korea Town: themed zones with concentrated Japanese and Korean dining and retail concepts.
- Large central activity/event spaces and outdoor/terrace dining areas.
- Ayala Malls Cinemas multiplex with premium formats (e.g., large-format screen and Dolby Atmos in select theaters).
- Broad mix of international and local brands, services, dining, and family/entertainment venues. Specific tenants and anchors change over time.

Access and transport
- Easy access by car via Macapagal Blvd./Asean Ave./Diokno Blvd.; close to NAIA.
- Served by city buses/jeepneys and app-based transport; terminal/stop arrangements can change.
- The planned LRT-1 Cavite Extension includes the Asia World station in the general area (under construction as of recent updates), which is expected to improve rail access once operational.

Community and events
- Regularly hosts pop-ups, cultural events, concerts, fairs, and seasonal installations.
- Was used as a vaccination site by local government during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Visitor notes
- Typical mall hours in Metro Manila are around 10 a.m.–9/10 p.m., but hours can vary by day, tenant, and season.
- Ayala Malls generally implement pet-friendly policies (often with a pet pass); check on-site rules.
